'''Lin Zunqi''' ({{zh|c=林尊琪}}; 3 June 1942 – 28 May 2018) was a Chinese physicist who was an expert in high-power [[solid-state laser]]s. He was a professor of the [[Shanghai Institute of Optics and Fine Mechanics]], chief engineer of the National Laboratory on High Power Laser and Physics of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] (CAS), and an academician of the CAS.<ref name="hlhl">{{Cite web|url=http://www.hlhl.org.cn/english/showsub.asp?id=580|title=Lin Zunqi|last=|first=|date=|publisher=[[Ho Leung Ho Lee Foundation]]|access-date=2018-06-07}}</ref>

Lin was born in [[Beijing]] on 3 June 1942.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.casad.ac.cn/doc/17642.html|title=林尊琪院士|last=|first=|date=|website=Chinese Academy of Sciences|access-date=2018-06-19}}</ref> After graduating from [[University of Science and Technology of China]] in 1964, he finished his postgraduate studies in 1968. He was instrumental in the construction of the [[Shenguang-II High Power Laser Facility]], China's largest [[laser fusion]] facility.<ref name="hlhl" /> He published more than 200 papers and won multiple national science prizes for his contributions to laser research. He was awarded the [[Ho Leung Ho Lee Prize]] for technological sciences.<ref name="hlhl" />

On 28 May 2018, Lin died at [[Huadong Hospital]] in [[Shanghai]], at the age of 75.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.cas.cn/xb/gz/201805/t20180529_4647590.shtml|title=中科院院士林尊琪逝世|last=|first=|date=2018-05-29|publisher=Chinese Academy of Sciences|access-date=2018-06-07}}</ref>
